_about: Every value the hardware rests on that the maker hasn't confirmed or that isn't from a citable table. One place: spec/hardware.py and tools/strength.py read these by id, reports/strength.md and reports/checks.md print them. To replace one: change its value and status here, and run the checks. status: 'assumed' until someone confirms it. basis: 'drawing' or 'catalogue' = read from the named document; 'standard practice' = a rule of thumb with no document behind it here; 'estimate, from memory' = a hand figure not checked against any document in this repo, so treat it as such.

rows.source: RS04 User Manual 260713 section 1.1: 9-M5 6.5 MIN. User's choice, 2026-11-05: design to the drawing
rows.replaces: STEP's 3.5 mm flat-floored bore, a shrink-wrap that may be cut short
rows.risk: If the STEP is right, engagement falls from 6 to 3 mm, 0.6 x d: thread strip then limits preload (reports/strength.md shows the margin)

rows.source: User's rule, 2026-11-05: no load on rear threads that are not on a drawing. RS04's rear 10-M4 is on its drawing; RS03 and RS06 rear ears and RS02's through-holes are not

rows.source: User's rule, 2026-11-05. Proof and breaking loads: ISO 898-1 via hardware_catalog.json (wuerth p3)
rows.risk: RobStride gives no grade or torque. A softer hub thread may need less

rows.source: Usual target for reusable joints (Shigley, VDI 2230 practice)
rows.risk: Scatter in tightening is about +-25 % with a torque wrench: separation margins carry it

rows.source: Black-oxide steel screw, dry or lightly oiled (Shigley)
rows.risk: Sets the torque quoted, not the capacities

rows.source: Bare aluminium on aluminium for slip, as tools/strength.py BOLT_SLIP_N already used
rows.risk: Anodised or oiled faces can be lower: slip margins scale with it directly

rows.unit: share of external tension the screw sees
rows.source: Typical screw in short metal clamp (VDI 2230 range about 0.1 to 0.3)
rows.risk: Small: tension margins are mostly preload

rows.source: 6061-T6 shear strength (ASM). RobStride's housing and hub alloys are unknown
rows.risk: A casting (ADC12 about 185 MPa, estimate) drops the strip margin by a tenth

rows.source: 7075-T6 shear strength (ASM)
rows.risk: Only for threads tapped in our own parts

rows.source: Same factor as tools/strength.py SF_MIN. The stripping area is the standard one for an internal thread (ISO 898 / FED-STD-H28), which assumes even load across the threads; first threads carry more
rows.risk: The check limits preload by this; it does not model fatigue of the thread
rows.settled_by: Bossard calculator for the alloy, or a pull test

rows.source: hardware_catalog.json thread_engagement.aluminium (project rule, top of Bossard F.044's range)
rows.risk: RobStride's threads are shallower than this by drawing: see the 'fastener' group

rows.source: Twice ISO 2768-m's +-0.1 mm for parts this size: the least running gap that is still a gap once made
rows.risk: Stack of three parts can use it up

rows.source: IKO CAT-57166 p8: on Super Slim, 'fit based on the actual measured dimensions' and 'a slight interference fit'. Seats are drawn at nominal diameter
rows.risk: Interference eats internal clearance at 70 to 90 %: machined to the bearing in hand

rows.value: 2 bearings, lever rule; the motor's own bearing takes none
rows.source: RobStride publishes no output bearing rating, so nothing is rested on it (reports/actuator_interfaces.md). Real share goes by stiffness: the motor's bearing will take some, which helps the two supports and loads it unrated
rows.risk: HIGH: knee capacities assume the fork shares load between the two supports only, with no flex in 3 mm cheeks
rows.settled_by: RobStride question 2; FEA of the fork

rows.value: the ankle motor's rated torque limits the lever
rows.source: A load repeated every step can only be held by what a motor sustains: RS06 rated 11 N m x 1.32 linkage, so 18 mm at 810 N. Static cases keep the peak
rows.risk: A faster walk or jog passes 810 N (reports/strength.md: to 2,220 N)

rows.source: IKO CAT-57166 Table 5: 1.2 to 1.5 normal operation, 1.5 to 3 with shock. Walking taken at the boundary
rows.risk: Shock loads would use a higher factor

rows.source: IKO CAT-57166 Table 4: 1.5 or more for normal operation
rows.risk: A fall isn't in the load cases at all

rows.source: 8 h a day x 1 cycle a second x 365 days x 3 years: a hand figure for a service life, no product requirement behind it
rows.risk: A real duty cycle may be half or twice this

rows.source: Knee swing in a calm walk (human about 60 deg). Not measured on echo's take
rows.risk: Enters the oscillating-life formula as a straight factor

rows.value: torso 0.42, thigh 0.70, shank 0.30, gaiter 0.24 of 3.3 kg/m2
rows.source: Iteration 41: the garment's density held 2.5 kg/m2 of undesigned formers. The shank's closed body now fills that skin to 3 mm, and the thigh needs only ribs off its tube. Knit 0.5 and foam 0.3 kg/m2 are the note in spec/robot.py MATERIALS
rows.risk: Up to 1.0 kg on the robot if formers are heavier than this. Nothing here is weighed
rows.settled_by: Design the thigh's ribs; a coupon of the knit and foam

rows.value: threaded rings M68 x 1, nut M50 x 1
rows.source: Thin rings, made not bought. Thread forms aren't drawn: the rings and nut are plain bands in the spec. Tightened with a pin spanner, locked with thread adhesive
rows.risk: Race axial load on a fine thread in 7075: not calculated; a circlip needs 2.65 mm of groove and 4 mm more width each side, estimate
rows.settled_by: FEA of the collar; a trial fit

rows.value: paste in the bore, gap pad on the skirt
rows.source: reports/strength.md counts these as contact area. No resistance is modelled, and the bore's 0.05 mm gap is a nominal
rows.risk: Rated torque isn't transferred from the maker's plate

rows.source: Steel, for screw masses: geometry times density, as no maker's mass table was read
rows.risk: None that matters

rows.value: upper and heel 1.5 mm TPU (wall_fill 0.5); midsole 0.45 of its solid; the outsole's top not counted
rows.source: Iteration 43: the shell rule gave the shoe a 3 mm wall, the midsole was a solid filling the whole shoe below its rail, frame included, and the outsole counted a top wall the midsole sits on. A molded shoe upper is about 1.5 mm; a midsole is foam under and round the frame, not through it
rows.risk: About 0.25 kg a foot if the shoe is built as the old rule counted it

rows.value: CuSn8 flanged bushings d10 D12, 5 and 6 long; pins d10 h6 hardened; shoulder screws ISO 7379 d6 12.9
rows.source: Iteration 43: plain bushings where a catalogue bearing would not fit the 5 to 6 mm plates. Allowable static pressure of bronze about 60 MPa, from memory: at 810 N on two, 6.8 MPa; at 3,400 N with the line off centre, 44 MPa
rows.risk: Wear and play over time, not strength; a polymer bushing of the same size if lubrication is a problem
rows.settled_by: A wear test on the bench

rows.value: female spherical rod ends, bore 6, eye 15, width 5 to 6, misalignment 15 deg or more
rows.source: Iteration 43: drawn to the size a catalogue M6 rod end has; static rating about 10 kN, from memory, against 2,649 N at the RS03's peak through the crank
rows.risk: The roll rod's lower end tilts 17 deg across its pin at full roll: a high-misalignment rod end
rows.settled_by: Pick a part from a catalogue
